conviction_note: A full-year print whose headline is the first FY2027 guide, and that guide will be the first company number ever to contain a full Champions League season PLUS two sponsorships signed in August and September 2026 that post-date every model and every word the company has spoken (last guidance 27 May 2026); the reported Q4 itself should read as a revenue miss against a consensus that sits above the company's own guide-implied maximum, which is why print_vs_bar_pct is negative while expected_move_pct is positive — the line this name has paid on is the guide (+12.68% on the 2026-05-27 raise) and it is the guide that steps up here, into a book with 8.0% of a 38.19m-share float short and 9.25 days to cover; sized above the finding sum (+4.5) because the rebuilt earnings base rate for this name is 7-13% per print, not the 1.8% the baseline's mis-matched 6-K history implies, and because the two sponsorship deals and the short book are one mechanism rather than two additive ones.
bar: Company's own raised FY2026 guidance of revenue GBP655-665m and adjusted EBITDA GBP200-210m, with nine-month revenue already reported at GBP520.1m — both from the Q3 FY2026 release filed as a 6-K exhibit, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1549107/000110465926066584/tm2615476d1_ex99-1.htm (2026-05-27). That arithmetic implies Q4 revenue of GBP134.9-144.9m. The sell-side bar is Q4 revenue of GBP148.17m / $192.226m (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/manchester-united-earnings-on-deck-champions-league-boost-in-focus-93CH-4911041, 2026-09-22, agreeing with https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/manchester-united-plc-announces-fourth-quarter-fiscal-2026-earnings-report-date-2026) and FY revenue of GBP665.16m, i.e. the exact top of the guided range.
positioning_check: 3.07m shares short, 10.54% of 172.43m shares outstanding and 8.04% of the 38.19m-share float, short ratio 9.25 days to cover, up from 2.77m the prior month (+10.8%): https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/manu/statistics/, read 2026-09-22. ADV is 332k-341k shares, so the short book is nine sessions of volume against a float that is 22% of shares outstanding. The baseline carries skew_25d_vol_points as null; put/call open interest is 1.86 but on total open interest of 1,201 contracts with an ATM bid-ask spread at 66.7% of mid, so the chain makes no directional statement I can use — the ~10.04% event-implied move is indicative only and I am not treating the put tilt as information. Shorts building 11% into a print whose headline is a record forward guide is the squeeze mechanism, and it is the reason both negative findings below are sized small.

findings.finding: The sell-side Q4 bar is arithmetically above what the company's own guidance allows: nine-month revenue is GBP520.1m and full-year guidance is GBP655-665m, so the guided Q4 is GBP134.9-144.9m, while consensus Q4 is GBP148.17m and consensus FY is GBP665.16m — the top of the range to the penny. Manchester United can only meet consensus by exceeding a guide it raised on 27 May with five weeks of the fiscal year left.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The directly comparable event is last year's full-year print, 2025-09-17: Q4 FY2025 revenue GBP164.1m against a GBP169.96m estimate, a 3.4% miss, with adjusted EPS of -3.16p against +7.14p expected, and the stock fell roughly 7.4% in pre-market (https://www.chartmill.com/news/MANU/Chartmill-34431-Manchester-United-PLC---CL-A-NYSEMANU-Reports-Q4-and-Full-Year-2025-Earnings-Misses-EPS-Estimates). The identical shape — sell-side Q4 above the guide-implied residual, seasonally empty April-June quarter — produced a mid-single-digit down move once. Sized at only -1.5 because it lands INSIDE a range the company published four months ago (lesson 6) and because a crowded short is a reason to shrink a negative (lesson 7).
findings.why_not_priced: This is a two-analyst name and the consensus is a mechanical -9.76% year-on-year roll of last year's GBP164.1m Q4 rather than a residual off the company's own guide; if the market had done the subtraction, the previews would be framing a GBP135-145m quarter rather than quoting GBP148.17m as the number to beat, and the FY estimate would not sit at exactly the top of a range the company gave itself. The same arithmetic gap existed a year ago and resolved as a printed 'revenue miss'.
findings.independence: Two independent estimate sources agree on the level being above the guide-implied maximum — Investing.com's GBP148.17m (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/manchester-united-earnings-on-deck-champions-league-boost-in-focus-93CH-4911041, 2026-09-22) and the $192.226m carried by the Nasdaq/MarketBeat feed. Both rest on the same underlying consensus, so treat them as one bar and two witnesses, not two facts; the guide-implied residual is from a different document (the 6-K exhibit).

findings.finding: Two commercial deals were signed AFTER the 30 June 2026 balance-sheet date and after the company last gave guidance on 27 May 2026, and both land only in the FY2027 outlook this release will introduce: a Betway training-kit partnership at a record ~GBP20m a year, which the club itself calls the biggest training-kit deal in world football (4 August 2026), and a SumUp shirt-sleeve deal the club calls its biggest ever sleeve partnership, against a prior DXC sleeve deal in the GBP10-20m a season range (8 September 2026).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance is the line this stock has actually paid on. On 2026-05-27, the one unambiguous earnings reaction in the baseline, Manchester United raised FY2026 revenue guidance to GBP655-665m and adjusted EBITDA to GBP200-210m and the stock rose +12.68% — the largest move in the eight-row history by a factor of nearly three. The 2025-09-17 full-year print guided FY2026 to GBP640-660m, BELOW the GBP666.5m just reported, and fell ~7.4%. Same name, same line, opposite signs, both double-digit-capable: the guide direction is the reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Both were sponsorship-trade and football-press stories, not financial-wire stories, and the equity market visibly did not reprice on them: the stock fell in 9 of the 10 sessions to 2026-09-10 and is -13.76% over 20 sessions, straight through the 8 September SumUp announcement, and is -15.5% from its 52-week high. If these were in the price, a name with a 38m-share float would not have made new short-term lows in the week its biggest-ever sleeve deal was signed. With two analysts covering and the last published model dated 27 May 2026 (Seeking Alpha's FY27 build, which lists only Champions League money, sporting bonuses and the Adidas clause), no sell-side FY2027 number can contain either deal. Combined they are roughly GBP20-30m of incremental, near-100%-margin annual commercial revenue against an adjusted EBITDA base of GBP200-210m.
findings.independence: The SumUp deal is a separate document and a separate date from the Betway one: https://insidersport.com/2026/09/08/manchester-united-sumup-sponsorship/ (2026-09-08), corroborated by https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/man-utd-agree-multi-million-101301094.html. The Betway deal is separately reported at https://www.insideworldfootball.com/2026/08/04/man-utd-agree-betway-training-kit-deal/ (2026-08-04). Both dates confirmed from the URL path, not the snippet. Net of the rest of the company (lesson 9): the offsetting question is whether broadcasting falls — it cannot, because FY2027 contains a full Champions League league phase against zero European football in FY2026, so commercial upside is additive rather than a mix shift.

findings.finding: 8.04% of a 38.19m-share free float is short with 9.25 days to cover — the highest days-to-cover in the day's universe — and the position was built by 10.8% in the last month, into a print at which the company is near-certain to introduce a record FY2027 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline's eight-row history is not earnings (the sweep set baseline_history_trustworthy false and the 10-day inferred cadence is impossible for a quarterly reporter), so the base rate is rebuilt from the two confirmed releases: +12.68% on 2026-05-27 and roughly -7.4% on 2025-09-17. This name moves 7-13% on a real print, and the 1.8% median in the baseline is a measurement of club operational 6-Ks, not of earnings. A 332k-share ADV means a covering short cannot get out inside the exit window.
findings.why_not_priced: The float is the unpriced part. Class A outstanding is 172.43m but the tradeable float is 38.19m after the Glazer Class B holding and the INEOS stake, so the quoted 10.54%-of-outstanding figure that screens and previews carry understates the real squeeze pressure by a factor of 2.6. Nothing in the baseline carries short interest at all, the option chain has 1,201 contracts of total open interest and a 66.7%-of-mid spread so it offers no hedge and no directional read, and the last four weeks of tape (-13.76%) are consistent with a short adding into a name nobody is defending. If the squeeze risk were priced, the chain would not be this empty and the borrow would show in a wider put skew rather than a null one.
findings.independence: Independently, the sweep row records the same 3.07m / 10.54% / 9.25 days figure and notes days-to-cover is the highest of the eight names it screened. The float number and the short number come from one page, so treat this as one document; the corroboration that the shorts are pressing rather than static is the month-on-month move from 2.77m to 3.07m on that same page.

findings.finding: The 10 June 2026 private placement of $550m of 5.36% senior secured notes due 2031, used to prepay the 3.79% notes due 2027, roughly doubles cash interest on the notes from about $16m to about $30m a year and adds $125m of net new principal — a real FY2027 drag on the net result that an adjusted-EBITDA guide will not show, plus write-off of unamortised issue costs on the prepaid notes in the reported quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean reaction in the record to a MANU financing event; the two 6-K dates nearest the June financing in the baseline (2026-06-12, -1.36% and 2026-06-22, -2.10%) are small and are not confirmed to be the refinancing. That is precisely why this is sized at -0.5 and not larger.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced as a headline and unpriced as arithmetic: the deal was covered as 'maturities extended', and the +$14m a year of cash interest does not appear in either of the two numbers the company guides on (revenue and adjusted EBITDA), so a record FY2027 EBITDA guide can print while the net-loss line and free cash flow stay where they are. If the market had done this arithmetic the previews would be discussing interest cover rather than only the Champions League revenue pool.
findings.independence: I asked the financing question rather than assuming distress, and the answer is a ramp, which is why this carries a small negative and not a large one: the $125m of net new money sits against GBP145m of disclosed incoming transfer fees in the summer 2026 window (https://psrwatch.com/insights/man-utd-summer-2026-transfer-window-review), a return to the Champions League group stage, and a squad-cost ratio of 56.7% against an 85% threshold — visible demand and visible use, not covenant pressure. The negative sized here is only the interest arithmetic; no distress reading is included.

searched_and_found_nothing: Whether the Hojlund permanent transfer to Napoli (EUR44m / ~GBP37m) completed before or after 30 June 2026 — it matters because a pre-30-June completion puts roughly GBP10m of profit on disposal into the reported quarter against a -GBP0.20 adjusted EPS consensus. Search snippets say 'early June 2026' but manutd.com returns HTTP 403 and I could not confirm the date from a primary document or a URL path, so I dropped the finding rather than build on an unverified date.

Any dated Old Trafford stadium financing decision inside the exit window — the GBP2bn / 100,000-seat project is live and the club and the freightliner remain apart on the land valuation, but nothing carries a date on or before 2026-09-23, so it is neither a finding nor an outside_window item.
A published FY2027 revenue or adjusted EBITDA consensus — none exists in any source I could reach, which is itself why the guide is the unpriced object here.
Any dividend or buyback signal ahead of the print; dividends have been suspended since 2022 and nothing in the record points to reinstatement at this release.
Glazer stake-sale specifics behind the 'sale speculation' in the 2026-09-17 TipRanks piece — no named buyer, no process, no date; rumour with no document, so worth 0.
A 25-delta skew reading: the baseline carries it null and the chain is too thin (1,201 contracts, 66.7%-of-mid ATM spread) to reconstruct one.
baseline_tension: It cuts against the 20-day run-up (-13.76%) and against the put-tilted open interest, and it agrees with nothing in the baseline except the size of the implied move: the tape says this name has been sold into the print, and my read is that what was sold is a reported quarter that will indeed look light, while the line that has actually paid on this name — the forward guide — steps up by more than any model contains, with the shorts nine days of volume away from the exit.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (positioning is the thing to beat, a crowded short shrinks a negative): shrank the Q4 revenue-miss finding from -3.0 to -1.5 given 8.04% of a 38.19m float short at 9.25 days to cover, and added the explicit sentence that the 1.86 put/call ratio on 1,201 contracts with a 66.7% spread is not a directional statement I am overriding.

Lesson 8 (thin coverage means a confirmed fact moves more, and understatement is the systematic error): raised the Betway/SumUp guidance finding from +3.0 to +4.0 — two company-confirmed, dated, unmodelled commercial contracts on a two-analyst name is the exact setup the lesson describes, and I had sized it below the name's own reaction distribution.

Lesson 4 (financing is a question, sign it after the answer): asked what the $125m of net new money buys, found GBP145m of summer transfer spend, a Champions League return and a 56.7% squad-cost ratio against an 85% threshold, so the distress reading is wrong; shrank the financing finding from -1.0 to -0.5 and restricted its text to the interest arithmetic only, with the ramp answer stated in independence.

Lesson 6 (a finding inside the guided range is a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect): reframed the Q4 finding as consensus sitting outside the company's own guide rather than the company missing anything, which is part of why it shrank, and recorded the bar as a company guide plus two agreeing estimate sources so no size cap applies.

Lesson 3 (your own caveat has to reach the number) and the 'read the set' rule: dropped the Hojlund profit-on-disposal finding entirely rather than carry a size on a date I could not confirm from a URL path, and resolved the financing finding to one sign instead of leaving both directions in it.

The foreign-private-issuer note ('a reaction history built from the wrong events is worse than none'): rebuilt the base rate from the two confirmed releases (+12.68% on 2026-05-27, ~-7.4% on 2025-09-17) rather than the baseline's 1.8% median, which is what let expected_move_pct rise from +3.5 to +5.0 against a finding sum of +4.5.

Lesson 1 kept print_vs_bar_pct and expected_move_pct deliberately opposite in sign and the conviction_note now says why: the fundamental read on the reported quarter is a miss, the reaction read is the guide.
